#3260. The Nvidia Scandal Has Been Brewing for Years. Here’s a Timeline

The Nvidia scandal seemed, for a moment, to be the straw that broke the back of the AI bubble. The stock valuation of the tech giant — a lynchpin in the wider tech economy — had plummeted, and dragged down the markets with it. The corporate line of succession was not clear and the allegations of wrongdoing and of a government cover up were already spilling over into the president’s Cabinet. Drastic measures would need to be taken to avoid a calamity.

On Monday, Donald Trump announced that he personally had persuaded the board of Nvidia to reinstate disgraced CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned earlier this month after admitting to an affair with an accused Chinese spy, through whom the company is accused of violating anti-China export controls on Nvidia’s hardware. “I believe my intervention was very important,” Trump said Monday, as the chip manufacturer’s stock price soared and major tech figures — now reassured of their control of the American economy and that Trump will shield them from potential corporate and federal oversight — celebrated Huang’s return.

The move is a stunning intervention by an American president in the operations of a private company, and part of a clear effort by the Trump administration to sweep the scandal and its potential fallout under the proverbial rug. While Huang is — at least for now — back in charge at the company he founded, questions remain about his credibility, his and the company’s legal and financial exposure, and what sort of promises were made to secure the board’s approval for the reinstatement.

The scandal feels like it unfolded overnight, but the chaos of the last month has been brewing for over two years, involving multiple government agencies, congressional committees, nations, and public figures.

Jensen Huang, according to The Wall Street Journal, meets Alice Huang — executive at the Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed — at an event in California. They are later photographed together at a bar in Taipei.  Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Per a Trump administration timeline, the U.S. Commerce Department opened an investigation into Megaspeed sometime in 2024, probing allegations that the Singapore-based data center company was violating U.S. export controls by facilitating sales of Nvidia chips to Chinese buyers by diverting them through third-party nations with less-stringent regulations. Customers of Megaspeed include Tencent and Alibaba.

Nvidia — like many other Silicon Valley players — donates $1 million dollars to the inauguration fund of the newly reelected Donald Trump.

The personal relationship between Trump and Huang ostensibly begins a few weeks after the president is sworn in for his second term, when the two men meet in person at the White House. Two days before, Trump made a large purchase of Nvidia stock worth between $1 and $5 million.

Chinese national Ling Mi, a business associate of Alice Huang and her husband Kang Wei, is charged with participating in a scheme to funnel Nvidia chips to China through Malaysia.

Huang attends a fundraising dinner for the MAGA Inc. PAC at Mar-a-Lago. The seat price is $1 million per person.  Related Content Donald Trump Rants About 'Radical Far Left,' Ballroom Critics in Thanksgiving Post Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie Settle Bitter Winery War That Detailed Abuse Claims Coachella Sues Walmart Over Unauthorized Festival Merch, Citing ‘Willful and Repeated Acts' Cardi B and Offset See Beverly Hills Mansion Lawsuit Dismissed After Settlement

Trump reverses course on a proposal to restrict the sale and export of Nvidia’s H20 chips  to the Chinese market.

The House Select Committee on China, controlled by Republicans, opens an investigation into whether Nvidia had provided the Chinese AI company Deepseek with access to their products in violation of export controls.

The Commerce Department requests records from Nvidia related to direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed.

The Commerce Department, under the supervision of Secretary Howard Lutnick, reverses a Biden-era set of export control protocols that — among other things — sought to restrict the export of high-performance chips and processors to adversarial nations.

The same day Lutnick reversed the Biden era rule, Huang embarked with Trump on a two-day trip to Saudi Arabia — where he committed to selling 18,000 chips to the kingdom as part of a data center development project.

Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are photographed and filmed together at a dinner in Taipei. Alice is seen kissing Huang on the cheek, and the two left the event together.

Nvidia places Megaspeed on its “no-sell list,” according to a timeline provided by the Trump administration. Agents of the Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security conduct an in-person inspection of Megaspeed’s Singapore facilities that same month.

Reporting from Bloomberg later found that while Megaspeed was on the “no-sell” list, the company continued to import thousands of Nvidia chips through the Malaysian market.

Singaporean authorities seize Alice Huang’s passport as their investigation into Megaspeeds compliance with international and national export laws unfolds .

Huang and Trump meet at the White House ahead of a trip to China by the Nvidia CEO. Contemporaneous news reports from the meeting note that the company had been working to negotiate favorable export control policies with the Trump administration. The following week, Huang announces that the company had secured permission to ramp up its production of restriction-compliant H20 chips for the China market — the sale of its most high end products, including the Blackwell and Rubin series, remain barred from export to China.

Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter contacted Commerce Department investigators seeking details related to the ongoing investigation into Megaspeed’s business dealings. Teter claimed that Jeff Kessler, Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security and a deputy to Lutnick, had given him his blessing to do so. The outreach raised alarm within the investigative unit about what sort of discussions Nvidia was engaging in with administration officials. The case was quickly transferred to the DOJ in order to avoid a suggestion of interference or impropriety.

Nvidia and semiconductor manufacturer Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD), announce an agreement to hand over 15 percent of revenue gained from AI hardware sales to China to the U.S. government, in exchange for export approval.

Days later, the president purchases between $5 and $25 million in Nvidia stock.

Alice Huang formally leaves Megaspeed. While Megaspeed publicly confirmed her departure, subsequent reporting suggests Huang may have continued to be involved in the operations of Megaspeed, albeit in an informal role.

Huang accompanies Trump on another international trip, this time to the United Kingdom, where the president and former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer sign a deal for a research partnership and standards-development framework for AI models between the two nations.

Nvidia quietly contributes $25 million to Trump’s White House ballroom construction project, becoming one of the largest corporate contributors to the controversial project. The donation was revealed a year later, in documents obtained by The Washington Post.

According to The New York Times, Trump is briefed on the Huang affair by U.S. intelligence officials, who describe Alice Huang as a “Chinese intelligence asset.”

The New York Times publicly reports on the American investigations into Nvidia and Megaspeed, and the alleged connections between Huang and Alice Huang.

Republican Senator Tom Cotton, of Arkansas, calls for an investigation into claims that Megaspeed was diverting Nvidia chips to China through its Singapore-based operations.

A compliance report filed by Nvidia to the U.S. government undercounts the number of chips sold to Megaspeed by over 50,000, according to trade records analyzed by Bloomberg. The total volume of product amounted to billions in trade volume.

Huang appears alongside other AI and Silicon Valley players — including Elon Musk — at a U.S.-Saudi investment forum held in Washington, D.C., pegged to a visit by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to the White House.

Trump praises Huang as a “smart man” following a meeting in 2026. Trump says Huang “knows” where the administration stands on export controls.

Trump announced that Nvidia will be allowed to sell its H200 AI chips — a newer model of chip that was still a far cry from its most advanced product —  to “approved” Chinese customers, in exchange for a 25-percent cut of revenue.

The exemptions granted by Trump the previous month formally go into effect. Nvidia praises the new rules and accuses Trump’s critics of “unintentionally promoting the interests of foreign competitors on U.S. entity lists.”

Alice Huang is expelled from Singapore and barred from reentering the county.

According to reporting from CNN, sometime in the spring of this year, the U.S. intelligence community intercepted communications indicating that an executive at Megaspeed was conducting an affair with a U.S. citizen. By this point, Alice Huang was already a person of interest.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio pens a memo to members of Trump’s Cabinet detailing concerns about Huang, his relationship with Alice Huang, and her alleged connections to Chinese intelligence, per The New York Times.

The White House releases a list of 11 individuals set to accompany Trump on a tech-focused trip to China. Huang is not included. The omission generates news coverage.

In an about face, Huang takes a late-night flight to catch up with Trump at a midterm campaign stop in Alaska. Shortly before Huang is set to join the president aboard Air Force One to fly to China, Rubio reportedly personally briefed Trump on intelligence obtained by the U.S. government suggesting that Huang’s mistress was a Chinese intelligence asset.

“Jensen is currently on Air Force One,” Trump wrote on Truth Social during the flight, “journeying to the Great Country of China where I will be asking President Xi, a Leader of extraordinary distinction, to ‘open up’ China so that these brilliant people can work their magic.”

Huang picks up a call from Trump during a taping of the All-In podcast at an AI summit in Los Angeles, and puts him on speakerphone for the audience. The two gush to each other.

“The robots will not be taking over. The AI will not be taking over the rest of the world. The whole thing is a hoax,” Trump said.

He added that any critics or detractors were  “just playing right into the hands of a lot of people that don’t want to see it happen. That could be political people, that could also be China.”

For his part, Huang said that he wouldn’t have picked up “if it wasn’t for you calling,” and that as it turns out “we were talking about you — good job sir.”

Huang is one of the signatories to a Trump-proposed pact among American AI and tech sector companies to “self police” AI development.

The New York Times breaks the news to the public that Huang may have been the target of a Chinese honeypotting scheme, and that American intelligence agencies, members of Trump’s Cabinet, and possibly the president, had been aware of the matter.

That same day, Huang denies any wrongdoing in relation to Nvidia’s relationship with Megaspeed, telling Bloomberg that “our relationship, our interactions, have been related to Megaspeed, and it was all completely normal and not unusual.”

In an email to Nvidia staff, Huang admits to having had an affair outside of his marriage. “Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation,” he writes. “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company.”

The New York Times reveals another affair with Nvidia Vice President of Health Care Kimberly Powell — one of Huang’s direct reports — and a violation of the company code of conduct.

Reuters reports that Huang had a second affair with an unnamed Nvidia employee.

Huang resigns from his position as Nvidia’s CEO. The company’s stock value falls sharply, shedding roughly half a trillion in market valuation over the course of the day.

When asked by reporters why Megaspeed was not placed on the federal government’s export blacklist — despite support from several agencies — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent throws Lutnick under the bus, telling reporters that ultimately “Commerce has the pen.”

The Financial Times reports that Huang’s allies in the tech industry have set up a “war room” to lobby for his reinstatement.

In a post on X, Huang addresses the reports that he is considering returning to Nvidia — despite, at that time, a lack of public support from the board.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he writes.

“I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A,” Trump writes on Truth Social.

The New York Times reports that Alice Huang had been in contact with an officer from China’s Ministry of State Security — the nation’s premier intelligence body — from between the spring of 2025 to the fall of this year. The time period overlaps with that of the alleged affair with Jensen Huang.

The Nvidia board announces that it has unanimously voted to reinstate Huang to his position as CEO. In a lengthy interview following the announcement, Trump claims that he “convinced” the board to do so.

Trump tells CNBC that Huang had been “exonerated” of any wrongdoing, a claim contradicted by Nvidia’s Monday statement, which said that the independent investigation into Huang’s alleged misconduct and national security vulnerabilities will “proceed to conclusion.”

A post from the President of the United States pic.twitter.com/mbOFMI6k0g

The Wall Street Journal reports that in order to convince the board to support Huang’s return, Trump had promised the company that the disgraced CEO and Nvidia were not the targets of investigations by the Department of Justice, headed by Trump’s personal lawyer Todd Blanche. Huang is scheduled to sit for a public hearing before the Senate Banking Committee.

#3259. IEEE Computer Society Chapter Offers Webinars With Industry Experts

Attendees in Region 4 learn about AI, cybersecurity, and more

Siva Rama Krishna Varma Bayyavarapu is an IEEE senior member and secretary of the IEEE Computer Society’s Central Indiana Chapter.

To help engineers keep up with emerging technologies such as AI, cloud computing, and sustainable infrastructure, and learn how they can be applied in practice, the IEEE Computer Society’s Central Indiana Chapter recently launched its Tech Talk Series.

The live webinar series connects IEEE members, undergrad and graduate students, and engineering professionals from IEEE Region 4 with industry practitioners. The monthly sessions have covered AI governance and security, agentic systems, and related topics. The sessions featured speakers from Apple, software company Tavant, and cybersecurity concern Zscaler.

Upcoming sessions and registration details are available on the IEEE Region 4 virtual events calendar.

Rather than presenting on emerging technologies only at a conceptual level, speakers discussed the design decisions behind specific tools and systems, how the systems are structured, and implementation challenges. They also shared lessons learned from using the tools in their daily work.

Sessions also include technical walkthroughs and practical examples.

The live format allows attendees to discuss and compare their approaches when evaluating and implementing new technologies with those used by other organizations.

The organizers chose to make the series virtual so that chapter members and other attendees could participate in technical discussions with engineers from major technology companies and eliminate the need to travel.

For young professionals, the sessions connect what they’ve learned in a classroom with the realities of the workplace.

Technical programs such as the Tech Talk Series give professionals and students access to expertise, help create connections across career levels, and make important engineering discussions available to a broader community.

Attendees learn how practitioners approach projects such as system architecture, reliability, security, governance, and product delivery. For experienced professionals, the talks offer a forum to examine new ways of designing, securing, and operating software systems, and compare technical approaches. They can ask questions relevant to systems being evaluated or deployed within their organization.

The most recent webinar, Feeding and Fencing AI Agents: Engineering Governed Agentic Systems on Real-Time Data, featured Gajendra Babu Thokala, a senior engineering leader at Apple in Seattle.

The IEEE senior member explained how teams can move beyond adding isolated AI features to applications and instead build governed AI-agent systems that use real-time business data to complete multistep business workflows.

Another recent session, Building AI Native Products: A Playbook for Agentic Systems, explored how products built around AI agents differ from traditional software. It also covered how agentic systems can help users complete multistep tasks and workflows. IEEE Senior Member Sandeep Shivam, a product and technology leader at Tavant in Dallas, led the webinar.

Those two sessions illustrate the series’ purpose: helping participants understand what a technology can do and what is required to use it responsibly.

Future sessions are being planned on areas including enterprise AI, software reliability, and responsible AI usage. In addition to speakers from technology companies, the chapter also plans to invite speakers from startups, universities, and research organizations.

Upcoming sessions are expected to cover cloud platforms, enterprise integrations, and the responsible development of AI systems.

Technical programs such as the Tech Talk Series give professionals and students access to expertise, help create connections across career levels, and make important engineering discussions available to a broader community.

Undergraduate and graduate students are invited to participate to gain exposure to technical decision-making and challenges encountered in professional engineering environments.

Siva Rama Krishna Varma Bayyavarapu is an IEEE senior member and the secretary of the IEEE Computer Society Central Indiana Chapter. He is also the chair of the IEEE Central Indiana Student Activities Committee.

You can now stream Nathan Fielder's fascinating and at times frustrating documentary "You Can See Everything" from the comfort of your couch, and pay at least $20 for the privilege. It's a sure bet for Best Documentary at the 2027 Oscars with a remarkable 97% on Rotten Tomatoes. If it were me, I'd wait until it comes to HBO Max in early 2027 — and save your hard-earned cash for the next entry in this list.

In our "You Can See Everything" review, my colleague called it "a bold, innovative documentary from alt-comedy creator Nathan Fielder and nonfiction filmmaker Lance Oppenheim, offering a fascinating look at convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes." The notorious tech-industry scammer has an acute allergy to self-reflection and proves nearly as manipulative as Fielder himself as the two get closer with the clock ticking down to her prison sentence.

Buy or rent "You Can See Everything" on Amazon now

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Now if you're dead set on relieving yourself of $25 to "own" a movie, "Wicker" is the clear choice for the horniest among us. I saw this in theaters with the girlies, and oh, how we cackled. Olivia Colman is as darling as ever as the prickly fisherwoman, who shows up at the local basket weaver's (Peter Dinklage) door with a weird ask. One wicker husband, coming up!

Alexander Skarsgård is uncanny and charming as her (and the town's) new obsession. Until things go sideways once a little wicker baby shows up...with another woman. "Wicker" is a delightfully horny time, theatrical as all get out, and Dinklage is given leave to soliloquy to his hearts' content. What more could you ask for to wile away a chilly weekend evening?

I'm not the biggest WWII movie buff, but my husband's excited to queue this one up if he can take a break from his emotional support WWII documentaries. A new war drama based on Buzz Bissinger’s nonfiction book of the same name, "The Mosquito Bowl" follows four college football stars who join the swell of promising young lads enlisting in the United States Marine Corps after Pearl Harbor.

With the Battle of Okinawa on the horizon, the guys — played by Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, Ray Nicholson and Tom Francis — stage a football game that would become known as "The Mosquito Bowl" that proves a welcome break from the daily horror of the frontlines. "Friday Night Lights" and "Lone Survivor" director Peter Berg is at the helm of this one, so you know you're in for something memorable, at the very least.

When Tim (Andrew Garfield) and Polly (Claire Foy) move their family of five to the English countryside hoping for a simpler life, their children chance upon an enchanted tree full of kooky inhabitants that can transport them to dazzling new lands befit of a child's imagination. Based on Enid Blyton's beloved children's books, it stars Nicola Coughlan, Nonso Anozie and Jessica Gunning, with a screenplay penned by Paddington 2 co-writer Simon Farnaby.

I haven't seen this one yet, but name-drop "Paddington 2" and you know I'm sat. It's one of the greatest family movies ever made and the rare children's movie I will stand 10-toes down on. If "The Magic Faraway Tree" captures even an ounce of that same magic, we're in for a treat. Plus, Andrew Garfield never fails to be dreamy in these kinds of roles.

Watch "The Magic Faraway Tree" on HBO Max now

"Reacher" star Alan Ritchson has been popping up everywhere lately. He joins forces with Owen Wilson in Hulu's latest action-comedy "Runner" where he gets plenty of opportunities to throw a punch. Ritchson stars as Hank Malone, a former soldier thrown into a frantic race against the clock when a medical delivery lands him squarely in the crosshairs of a ruthless cartel. With an innocent child's life hanging in the balance, Hank's determined to get his cargo where it needs to go before it's too late.

Owen Wilson co-stars as his partner, alongside Rodrigo Santoro as a cartel member and Leila George, with Scott Waugh of "Need for Speed" and "Expend4bles" fame in the director's chair. "Reacher's" really been on a downward trend since season one, but Ritchson and Wilson play off each other well enough in this breezy popcorn watch. And that's exactly the kind of thing that's calling my name after inhaling Thanksgiving dinner.

#3256. Nothing's First Over-Ear Headphones Are $130 Off for Black Friday

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

Nothing's first over-ear headphones, the Headphone (1), is $130 off for Black Friday, bringing them down to $169 from $299 (their lowest price ever). Nothing's newer Headphone (a), which launched in 2026 and earned an "excellent" rating in PCMag's review, is on sale as well, dropping to $109 from $199. For more discounts and the latest offers, check out our extensive Black Friday 2026 coverage.

In line with the company’s design language, these headphones feature transparent elements and bold, geometric detailing that make them stand out from typical matte-black pairs. But the appeal goes beyond the look. These IP52-rated headphones use 40mm drivers, hybrid ANC, and both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. They also support high-res audio via LDAC, while Nothing’s companion app gives you basic and advanced EQ controls for adjusting the sound. Battery life is impressive, too, stretching to 35 hours with ANC on and up to 80 hours with it switched off.

But the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

That said, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. We expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.
